name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
flagName: Flag of Saint Pierre and Miquelon
summary: A blue field with a yellow ship sailing on waves, and a hoist band showing the flags of the Basque Country, Brittany and Normandy, the homelands of the islands' settlers. The flag is unofficial; officially the tricolour is used.
origin: The islands off Newfoundland are the last remnant of New France in North America. The flag, created in the early 1980s, honours the settlers' origins.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The ship, the Grande Hermine of Jacques Cartier.

symbols.name: Ship
symbols.meaning: The Grande Hermine, in which Jacques Cartier is said to have reached the islands in 1536.

symbols.name: Three regional flags
symbols.description: The Basque ikurriña, the Breton Gwenn-ha-du and the Norman two leopards.

facts: The islands are the only part of New France still under French rule.
They lie just 25 km from Newfoundland, Canada.
It is one of the few flags containing other flags.
clues: Blue with a yellow ship and three small regional flags at the hoist.
Its small flags honour Basque, Breton and Norman settlers.
The last remnant of New France.
